age.evidence: Adult male Wistar-Han rats (280-350 g; Charles River, Germany) were used.

sex.evidence: Adult male Wistar-Han rats (280-350 g; Charles River, Germany) were used.

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin was dissolved in 0.9% NaCl and administered subcutaneously (sc) at 1 mL/kg... During weeks 3-4 of CUMS exposure, both stressed and nonstressed animals received two injections of psilocybin (0.6 mg/kg, sc) or saline.

handling.evidence: Rats were handled once daily prior to experimentation.

group_housing.evidence: Animals were acclimated and housed six per cage in controlled conditions (note: CUMS stressors were applied individually and 'Control rats were housed separately', so housing during the CUMS period is somewhat ambiguous).

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12:12 h light-dark cycle (direction/lights-on time not stated).

enrichment_housing.evidence: Enriched housing was omitted to avoid potential confounds in pharmacological studies.

assays.assay_description: 1-h sucrose (1-2%) consumption sessions after 14 h food/water deprivation; seven baseline sessions, weekly monitoring across CUMS; tested 7 days after first and second psilocybin dose (0.6 mg/kg s.c.) in stressed and non-stressed rats; intake measured by bottle weighing.

application_type.evidence: two injections of psilocybin (0.6 mg/kg, sc) or saline

setup_habituation.evidence: Rats were trained to consume 1-2% sucrose solution during seven 1-h baseline sessions

setup_restrain.evidence: Sucrose intake was measured by weighing bottles before and after the test.

food_restriction.evidence: following 14 h food and water deprivation... only deprived of food and water during 14 h preceding each SPT

water_restriction.evidence: following 14 h food and water deprivation... only deprived of food and water during 14 h preceding each SPT

time_to_assay.evidence: The final SPT was performed seven days after the second psilocybin dose; Fig. 2: SPT 7 days after the first and the second dose injection.

outcomes.summary: CUMS reduced sucrose consumption (anhedonia). Psilocybin (0.6 mg/kg s.c.) reversed this deficit, significantly increasing sucrose preference in stressed rats 7 days after both the first and second dose.
outcomes.statistics: week 4: F(1,30) = 11.93, p < 0.0001; week 5: F(1,22) = 7.05, p < 0.002; stressed vs non-stressed saline p < 0.0002 (one-way ANOVA, LSD post hoc)
outcomes.evidence: Administration of psilocybin (0.6 mg/kg, sc) reversed this deficit, significantly increasing sucrose preference in stressed animals after both the first (week 4; F₁,₃₀ = 11.93, p < 0.0001) and the second (week 5; F₁,₂₂ = 7.05, p < 0.002) dose.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Sucrose intake was measured by weighing bottles before and after the test.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only session totals (bottle weights) reported; weekly comparisons are between-session.

B4_ethological.evidence: Consummatory intake measured by bottle weighing, not scored ethological acts.

B5_social.evidence: Assay does not target social behaviour.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Sucrose preference is a hedonic consummatory measure, not a learned task.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Sucrose intake was measured by weighing bottles.

E8_food_water.evidence: Sucrose intake was measured by weighing bottles before and after the test (fluid accessible during the session).

D1_continuity.evidence: seven 1-h baseline sessions... Weekly sucrose consumption was monitored throughout the experiment.

D3_recording_days.evidence: seven 1-h baseline sessions... Weekly sucrose consumption was monitored throughout the experiment.

D4_baseline.evidence: Animals were assigned to matched groups based on final baseline sucrose intake.

D5_followup.evidence: The final SPT was performed seven days after the second psilocybin dose

assays.assay_description: WDS episodes (rapid shaking of head, neck and trunk) counted for 60 min immediately after the first and second psilocybin injection (0.6 mg/kg s.c.), in 5-min bins by two independent observers; expressed as total episodes in stressed and non-stressed rats.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin was dissolved in 0.9% NaCl and administered subcutaneously (sc) at 1 mL/kg.

setup_restrain.evidence: WDS episodes were recorded for 60 min post-psilocybin by two independent observers (no restraint described).

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in observation setting.

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in observation setting.

time_to_assay.evidence: WDS test was performed immediately after the first and the second psilocybin injection.

sample_size.evidence: Values are the mean ± SEM (n = 7) (4 groups: stress/no stress × saline/psilocybin)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (0.6 mg/kg s.c.) significantly increased WDS in both stressed and non-stressed rats after each injection; authors report chronic stress did not alter the acute hallucinogenic-like response (although figure notes a stressed vs non-stressed psilocybin difference).
outcomes.statistics: F(3,48) = 33.73, p < 0.0001; psilocybin vs saline p < 0.05; psilocybin stressed vs non-stressed p < 0.0002 (two-way ANOVA, Tukey)
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin administration (0.6 mg/kg, sc) significantly increased the number of wet dog shake (WDS) responses in both stressed and nonstressed rats (Fig. 3). Statistical analysis revealed a robust treatment effect following each psilocybin injection (F₃,₄₈ = 33.73, p < 0.0001)

B1_num_measures.evidence: are expressed as the total number of episodes

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: recorded... in 5 min bins... and are expressed as the total number of episodes (bins not analysed).

B4_ethological.evidence: WDS/HTR is excluded from ethological behaviours by rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Assay does not target social behaviour.

D1_continuity.evidence: WDS test was performed immediately after the first and the second psilocybin injection.

D2_session_duration.evidence: WDS episodes were recorded for 60 min post-psilocybin

D3_recording_days.evidence: after the first and the second psilocybin injection (two days, 7 days apart)

assays.assay_description: Circular arena 1 m diameter, virtually divided into 8 sections, centre lit by 75 W bulb; 5-min observation 7 days after last psilocybin dose by two observers; walking time, centre time, line crossings, grooming, rearing, peeping.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were placed in the center... and were observed for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food in open-field arena described.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in open-field arena described.

time_to_assay.evidence: Rats were placed in the center seven days after the last drug injection

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin increased walking time and line crossings in stressed rats but decreased them in non-stressed rats; rearing increased in stressed rats, grooming increased in stressed but decreased in non-stressed rats, peeping unchanged; centre exploration increased in both groups.
outcomes.evidence: In the open field test (OFT), psilocybin increased the walking time and line crossings in stressed rats but decreased these measures in nonstressed animals... Center exploration was enhanced in both groups following psilocybin (F₁,₂₄ = 16.28, p < 0.0001).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Behavior was quantified as the time spent walking, time in the center, number of line crossings, grooming episodes, rearing episodes, and peeping under the arena.

B4_ethological.evidence: grooming episodes, rearing episodes, and peeping under the arena

B5_social.evidence: Assay does not target social behaviour.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: observed for 5 min by two independent observers

E6_spatial.evidence: virtually divided into eight sections (virtual zones only)

E7_social_context.evidence: Rats were placed in the center... and were observed for 5 min (individual testing not explicitly stated)

D3_recording_days.evidence: seven days after the last drug injection (single test day)

D5_followup.evidence: Rats were placed in the center seven days after the last drug injection

assays.assay_description: Light (white, open, 30×30×30 cm, 100 lx) and dark (black, closed, 30×30×30 cm) compartments connected by 10×10 cm tunnel; 5-min test starting in light compartment, 8 days after second psilocybin dose; time in each compartment and crossings scored by two observers.

setup_habituation.evidence: Animals were habituated to darkness for 1 h before testing (dark adaptation, not apparatus exposure).

setup_restrain.evidence: Each rat was tested individually for 5 min, starting in the center of the light compartment facing away from the tunnel.

time_to_assay.evidence: significantly reduced time spent in the dark compartment in stressed rats eight days after the second dose

outcomes.summary: Stressed rats spent more time in the dark compartment; psilocybin significantly reduced dark-compartment time in stressed rats 8 days after the second dose without changing crossings.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin (0.6 mg/kg × 2) significantly reduced time spent in the dark compartment in stressed rats eight days after the second dose (F₁,₂₄ = 19.16, p < 0.0001; Fig. 4), without affecting the number of crossings between compartments (F₁,₂₄ = 1.7, p < 0.19).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Time spent in each compartment and number of crossings were recorded

B4_ethological.evidence: Zone time and crossings are spatial measures.

B5_social.evidence: Assay does not target social behaviour.

E1_environment_type.evidence: The apparatus consisted of a light compartment... and a dark compartment

E6_spatial.evidence: light compartment... and a dark compartment... connected by a 10 × 10 cm tunnel

D1_continuity.evidence: Each rat was tested individually for 5 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: eight days after the second dose (single test)

D5_followup.evidence: eight days after the second dose

assays.assay_description: Two open arms (50×10 cm) and two closed arms (50×10×40 cm) elevated 40 cm; 5-min trial from centre, run on same day as LDB (~8 days after second dose); time in open and closed arms recorded manually by two blinded observers.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were placed in the center for a 5 min trial

time_to_assay.evidence: Behavioral tests (OF, LDB + EPM, FST) were conducted in 24 h intervals starting 7 days after the last psilocybin dose; LDB reported 'eight days after the second dose'.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin decreased closed-arm time in stressed rats with no change in open-arm time; no psilocybin effect in non-stressed rats. Saline stressed rats paradoxically spent more time in open arms than non-stressed controls.
outcomes.evidence: In the elevated plus maze (EPM) test, psilocybin decreased time spent in closed arms in stressed rats (F₁,₂₄ = 49.9, p < 0.0001), whereas time in open arms remained unchanged.

B1_num_measures.evidence: time spent in open and closed arms was recorded manually

B4_ethological.evidence: Arm time is a spatial measure.

B5_social.evidence: Assay does not target social behaviour.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: recorded manually by two blinded and independent observers

E1_environment_type.evidence: The EPM consisted of two open arms (50 × 10 cm) and two closed arms (50 × 10 × 40 cm)

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are part of apparatus design, not shelter (rubric).

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM arms are extensions of central platform (rubric: score 0).

E7_social_context.evidence: Rats were placed in the center for a 5 min trial (individual testing not explicitly stated)

D5_followup.evidence: Behavioral tests (OF, LDB + EPM, FST) were conducted in 24 h intervals starting 7 days after the last psilocybin dose administration

assays.assay_description: Cylinder 50 cm × 23 cm diameter, water 30 cm at 25 °C; 15-min pre-test swim then 5-min test 24 h later (>7 days after second dose); immobility, swimming and climbing scored by two blinded observers.

setup_habituation.evidence: On the pre-test day, rats swam for 15 min... Twenty four hours later, rats were retested for 5 min.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were placed individually in a cylinder (50 cm height × 23 cm diameter) filled to 30 cm with water

water_restriction.evidence: Water is the swim medium, not available for drinking.

time_to_assay.evidence: Behavioral tests (OF, LDB + EPM, FST) were conducted in 24 h intervals starting 7 days after the last psilocybin dose administration (exact FST day not stated).

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin reduced immobility in both stressed and non-stressed rats; in stressed rats swimming and climbing increased, while non-stressed rats showed increased swimming but reduced climbing.
outcomes.evidence: In the forced swim test (FST), psilocybin reduced immobility in both stressed and non-stressed rats (F₁,₂₄ = 6.93, p < 0.001). In stressed rats, active behaviors-swimming (F₁,₂₄ = 103.5, p < 0.0001) and climbing (F₁,₂₄ = 95.1, p < 0.0001)-were significantly increased by psilocybin

B1_num_measures.evidence: Two blinded and independent observers scored immobility, swimming, and climbing behaviors

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility excluded from ethological behaviours by rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Assay does not target social behaviour.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Behavioural despair test, not a learned task.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Two blinded and independent observers scored

E1_environment_type.evidence: cylinder (50 cm height × 23 cm diameter) filled to 30 cm with water

E7_social_context.evidence: Rats were placed individually in a cylinder

E8_food_water.evidence: water is the swim medium, not accessible for drinking

D1_continuity.evidence: Twenty four hours later, rats were retested for 5 min (only retest data scored/reported; pre-test is a conditioning swim).

D3_recording_days.evidence: only the 5-min retest day has reported data

D4_baseline.evidence: Pre-test swim occurred after dosing and its data are not reported.

D5_followup.evidence: starting 7 days after the last psilocybin dose administration

judge_notes: All three candidates identified the same six behavioural assays (SPT, WDS, OFT, LDB, EPM, FST); neurogenesis IHC, qRT-PCR BDNF and corticosterone ELISA excluded as non-behavioural.
B1 corrected per rubric points: single-measure assays (SPT, WDS) score 0 (gemma gave 1); OFT 6 measures = 4-6 → 2 (gemma gave 3); LDB 2-3 → 1 (qwen gave 0).
WDS B2 set to No against 2/3 modal: paper states bins were recorded but data 'expressed as the total number of episodes'; no within-session analysis reported.
WDS D1 set to Multiple (1) to match D3=2-7: Fig. 1/Fig. 3 show WDS recorded after both first and second injection, 7 days apart.
FST D1/D3 set to single session/1 day: 15-min pre-test is a conditioning swim with no reported data; consequently D2 <15 min and D4 No.
LDB setup_habituation set to not_reported: '1 h habituation to darkness' is dark adaptation, not apparatus exposure.
Time-to-assay: OFT 7 d (short_term), LDB stated 8 d (long_term_over7d), EPM run with LDB (11520 min, medium), FST >7 d but exact day not stated (value_minutes null).
SPT E8 = Yes (modal): sucrose/water bottles accessible during the 1-h session; SPT apparatus otherwise undescribed (low confidence E items).
day_night_flipped = not_reported: only bare '12:12 h light-dark cycle' stated.
n_total = 28 inferred from n = 7 per group across 2×2 stress × treatment design (medium confidence for WDS).
